notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after the first round of searches (one per candidate for the first nineteen names, none for the eleven sitting legislators). The rest was done by opening pages directly with the kit's own User-Agent: each campaign's own site, the Iowa Legislature's legislator pages, county and city sites, the Republican Party of Iowa's and the Polk County Democrats' own candidate pages, the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee's candidate pages, and two news articles. A voter guide (theballotbrief.com) was used only to find campaign site addresses; nothing is cited to it except the tie noted for Steve Simon.

Behind a wall, so not read and not recorded: charleythomsonforhouse.com (Charley Thomson) and roebuckforiowa.com (Karen Roebuck) both answered with a CAPTCHA redirect. Ballotpedia returned an empty page. Tom Walton's Bio page (waltonforiowa.com/bio) is drawn by script and showed no text, so no office is recorded for him.

The party pages recorded under endorsed_by are candidate lists, not statements using the word 'endorse': the Republican Party of Iowa's '2026 Candidates' page, the Polk County Democrats' 'Candidates 2026' page, and the DLCC's candidate pages ('with the support of the DLCC'). Each entry quotes what the page says so the second reader can judge whether it counts.

Steve Simon: the City of Waterloo's council page lists 'Steve Simon, At-Large Through 12/31/2027'. The tie between that council member and the supervisor candidate rests on the voter guide's summary of a Waterloo-Cedar Falls Courier report (he 'plans to keep that seat while running for county supervisor'); the Courier article itself was not opened. The second reader should confirm or remove.

Austin Baeth's site names him and House District 36 but still reads 'VOTE NOVEMBER 5', the 2024 election date. Liz Bennett's and Sandy Salmon's sites name the candidate and the Senate district but show no 2026 date.
Wikipedia's full birth dates for John Forbes and Chris Cournoyer were cut to the year. Dillon Fillion's full date is from his own campaign site.

Not recorded although seen: police and other employment (Mike Tupper, Randy Meier, Benjamin Mulford, Drew Stensland), party posts (Tom Walton, Samy El-Baroudi, Samantha Fett), nonprofit boards, student offices, and Chris Cournoyer's 'local school board' (her site gives no district or years). Endorsements by individual officeholders are not party endorsements and were left out.

Nothing citable was found for Bob Bartles, Stephen Doerscher, Ross Eveland, Thomas Jay Moore, Charley Thomson, Michael R. Bergan, Helena Hayes, Karen Roebuck, Matthew Rinker and Kevin Alons (the six sitting legislators among them already have record pages; no campaign website was found for them).

verifier_notes: Every url was re-opened with the kit's own User-Agent (drewforiowa.com, which answered 429 to it, was read with the reading tool instead). Linn County's elected-officials PDF was read as text: Treasurer, Brent C. Oleson, Democratic Party, 4 Year Term, Elected 11/8/2022, Term Expires 12/31/2026.

Party candidate lists (Polk County Democrats 'Candidates 2026', Republican Party of Iowa '2026 Candidates') were not counted as endorsements and were removed. The DLCC pages were kept because each says the candidate has 'the support of the DLCC', the Democratic Party's legislative campaign committee, on its own page for the November 3, 2026 race.

Sites that name the candidate and the office but show no 2026 date were kept as recorded, with that said in 'how': Julia Helm, Dustin Durbin, Carter F. Nordman, Dillon Fillion, Sandy Salmon, and Austin Baeth (still 'Vote November 5').
